commits.message:
A held renderable is drawn at no column, never a negative width (rich-protocol-9xcs.8te)

Review: a container's arithmetic can hand a child a negative or NaN width;
drawsNothing reads it as no column, but the held draw passed it through, so
Rule threw RangeError inside narrow Markdown lists and Constrain.

A held renderable is drawn and dropped; Composite.contents is gone (rich-protocol-9xcs.8te)

Under one column `render` used to walk `Composite.contents`, a second
description of each container's traversal kept beside its `render`, because
drawing used to commit state. Renders no longer write, so a held renderable
is now drawn in a phase whose effects are dropped (as a measurement's are),
its segments discarded, and everything it draws reported held. What a held
container holds is what it draws, under the options it hands each child — a
container rewriting `frame` included, which `contents` could not see.

Composite, isComposite and every contents method are deleted.
test/renderables/contents.test.ts becomes held.test.ts: every exported
renderable survives being drawn under one column and reports the probes it
reports drawn. A Table seats one column at no width and drops the rest, as at
any width too narrow for their dividers; contents had reported them all.

TextInput scrolls as a Viewport, layout kept once the frame is drawn (rich-protocol-9xcs.o76) (#509)

* TextInput scrolls as a Viewport, and keeps its layout once the frame is drawn (rich-protocol-9xcs.o76)

A TextInput's render wrote its visual rows, scroll window, single-line
window and drawn options into plain fields. Now the one fact only a render
learns — the width and ASCII-ness it drew under — is a State kept through
afterPass, and the rows and windows are derived from it and the current
value. The multiline scroll is a Viewport, so the cursor row is followed,
the wheel scrolls the field, and a handled key brings the caret back.

A Panel's bottomRightAccessory function is handed the rows its body drew,
and scrollIndicatorText(frame) counts the rows that frame laid out, read
off the field's own stamped cells: right on its first frame, on a resize,
and at any depth. The render-purity debt list is empty and deleted.

* TextInput reads each frame's layout off its cells; maxRows is a ceiling (rich-protocol-9xcs.o76)

High review pass on PR #509:
- A click maps through the layout stamped on the cell it lands on (WidgetMouseEvent.cell),
  not one recomputed from the cursor and value since.
- maxRows caps the viewport as a height ceiling instead of fixing its rows.
- The field is at least as wide as it measures, held to the offer, so a blank field
  keeps its minRows; with arrows it is exactly the offer.
- levelOf in core/anchor is the one owner-chain walk; Viewport's EMPTY is shared.

* TextInput keeps a caret past a full row under arrows, and an arrow keeps its cell's place (rich-protocol-9xcs.o76)

* TextInput draws only the rows in view, and reads a click off its frame's settings (rich-protocol-9xcs.o76)

Escalation high pass on PR #509:
- Viewport.showingLines shows content of known length that draws only the lines a
  frame shows; TextInput's frame costs O(maxRows) again (20k lines: ~175ms -> ~2ms).
- The field's width comes from the rows in view, so a frame no longer measures the
  whole value; graphemes() skips segmentation for printable ASCII, as cellLen does.
- A frame's layout carries what it was drawn under and, single-line, the value it
  showed, so a click maps through that frame alone.
- Stale accessory-thunk test comment and WidgetBase stamping comment corrected.
Review: the template frames test names FrameSequence, not the removed Frames (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

Review: the pulse test reads what Progress draws; one clock in the showcase (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

The BarColumn pulse test supplied its own frame and compared against a
literal 7.5; it now prints the Progress and compares each row to the bar
drawn in a frame for 7.5s. A test pins that, in a frame of its own host,
a Progress holds what it would draw. Spinner's placed renderable is built
in the constructor after the sequences it closes over. The showcase draws
the dashboard at the Live's frame time, so the heading and the jobs share
one clock. Two doc sentences that described examples no longer present
are corrected.

An animation is drawn one way: placed (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

Removes every public way to draw an animation at a time the caller names:
frameAt and its Stamped renderable, the Frames class, Spinner.drawnAt, and
ProgressBar's pulse: { t }, now pulse: true. A FrameSequence, a Spinner and a
pulse are placed and draw at the frame's time.

Progress draws its table in a frame of its own host's time when printed with
none, so the bars and spinners placed in it draw at the moment its tasks are
drawn at. Examples and docs place their animations; docs that played an effect
over frames at sampled moments now play it in a live fence.
